It directed agencies to pause refugee decisions and admissions, while allowing exceptions on a case-by-case basis when the government determined that admission served the national interest. The order also required recurring reports on whether refugee admissions might resume. This was a significant change to the refugee program, but its text does not abolish the separate asylum system, terminate Temporary Protected Status, cancel T or U visas, or consolidate immigration agencies. The linked immigration-policy analyses discuss Project 2025 proposals and broader concerns, which should remain distinct from what the order actually did. The pause therefore concerned admissions under this particular program, rather than every route to protection.
